headline: Single-cell and spatial maps reveal immune states in inflamed and tumor tissues
label: Single Cell Immune Profiling
summary: Current single-cell and spatial datasets resolve state-specific immune programs linked to therapy response, metastasis, and viral disease severity.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the use of single-cell, spatial, and integrative computational frameworks to resolve cell-state programs that track clinical outcome. Several items apply network or decomposition methods directly: CytokineLink reconstructs cytokine interaction networks from Crohn's disease scRNA-seq, implicating IL17C-driven modules and lost IL10 feedback in anti-TNF non-response, while PRISM-MM uses sparse integrative dictionary learning to extract conserved drug-response states in multiple myeloma. Others map state-specific populations in situ, including altered macrophage states in immunosuppressed skin cancer, a CAF subpopulation that recruits hyper-suppressive regulatory T cells in lung cancer, and immune escape pathways in prostate cancer bone metastases. The new element across these items is explicit linkage of cell-state architecture to treatment failure, metastasis, and viral severity. The genome-wide CRISPRa screen across 3.6M CD4 T cells adds a perturbation-level map of surface protein regulators.
